diagnostic_evidence.quote: To ensure the injectivity of the encoder approximated by a neural network, each layer must be injective, condition which is satisfied when $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$ for all hidden layers, so $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$ for $\ell = 1,\ldots,L-1$.
By \Cref{th:uap}, we have that $n_\ell = n_\text{in}+n_\text{out}$ is sufficient to satisfy $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ and $\lim_{|\myw|\to\infty}\Varepsilon_2 = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$ does not imply $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$. For example, $n_\text{in}=2$, $n_1=10$, $n_2=3$ satisfies $n_2\geq n_\text{in}$ but $n_2<n_1$, so the second layer cannot be injective. Even $n_\ell\geq n_{\ell-1}$ is insufficient without full-rank affine maps and injective activations. Moreover, the universal approximation theorem gives approximation, not exact representation, so it cannot establish $\Varepsilon_1=0$.

failure_location.quote: A sufficient condition for the width to ensure injectivity of the encoder is $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$, for $\ell = 1,\ldots, L-1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the condition to $n_\ell\geq n_{\ell-1}$ for all hidden layers, assume full-rank affine maps and injective activations, and separately prove the existence of an exact decoder or restrict the claim to approximation error $\Varepsilon_2$.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's guidance for designing autoencoders with null representation error, and the claim that generic manifolds can be exactly represented by non-linear autoencoders, are not established.
issues.title: False sufficient condition for encoder injectivity and null representation error
issues.why_classification: A comparable corrected sufficient condition exists, but the current theorem is false and requires nontrivial additional assumptions and a corrected proof.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The parameters $\mu$ vary in a compact set with non-empty interior $\mathcal{P}\subset \mathbb{R}^{a-1}$
the map $B_r((t^*,\mu^*)) \ni (t, \mu) \to u_N$ is injective $\forall (t^*, \mu^*) \in [0,T]\times\mathcal{P}$, with $r$ small enough.

issues.failure_explanation: The domain $[0,T]\times\mathcal{P}$ has boundary because $\mathcal{P}$ is compact with non-empty interior and $t$ is restricted to $[0,T]$. At boundary points, a neighborhood in the image is homeomorphic to a half-space, not to $\mathbb{R}^a$. The proof incorrectly concludes local Euclidean structure. The set is at best a manifold with boundary.

failure_location.quote: We conclude that $U$ is locally Euclidean, so $\{u_N(t;\mu)\}_{t\in[0,T], \mu \in \mathcal{P}}$ is a $a$-manifold, that we denote by $\mathcal{M}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim with '$a$-dimensional manifold with boundary' or restrict the analysis to the interior of $[0,T]\times\mathcal{P}$.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusion that $\mathcal{M}$ is an $a$-manifold without boundary is not justified; later embedding and reduction statements may need to be restated for manifolds with boundary.
issues.title: Solution set is a manifold with boundary, not a manifold
issues.why_classification: A short local correction preserves the dimension and the subsequent embedding results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Global injectivity can be obtained by augmenting the solution set with parameters and time, i.e. considering the set $\{(u_N(t;\mu), t, \mu)\}_{t \in [0,T],\, \mu \in \mathcal{P}}$
Thus, we can achieve the lowest latent size $n = a$.

issues.failure_explanation: $[0,T]\times\mathcal{P}$ is compact and cannot be homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^a$. More importantly, augmenting with $t$ and $\mu$ changes the input space. The method's encoder $\Psi'$ takes only $u_N$. If the original map $(t,\mu)\mapsto u_N$ is not globally injective, no function of $u_N$ alone can recover $t,\mu$. Thus the augmented graph can be embedded in $\mathbb{R}^a$, but this does not imply the original solution manifold can be encoded with latent size $a$.

failure_location.quote: By the injectivity and continuity of $(t,\mu)\to(u_N(t;\mu),t,\mu)$, and by the compactness of $\mathcal{P}$, follows that there exist a global homeomorphism to $\mathbb{R}^a$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either assume global injectivity of $(t,\mu)\mapsto u_N$, or state that the latent size $a$ applies to the augmented graph and requires $t,\mu$ as inputs.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed lower bound $n=a$ for the latent dimension is unsupported; it holds at best for the augmented set or under an additional global injectivity assumption.
issues.title: Augmenting with parameters does not justify latent dimension $n=a$ for the solution manifold
issues.why_classification: The false claim is contained in an observation, but it materially affects the advertised minimum latent dimension and requires a nontrivial additional assumption or correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We now assume the construction of an autoencoder that realizes an orthogonal projection.

issues.failure_explanation: Since $J_{\Psi'}$ is $n\times N$ with $N>n$, $J_{\Psi'}^\top J_{\Psi'}$ is $N\times N$ and singular, so its inverse does not exist. The correct right inverse/orthogonal projection decoder is $J_{\Psi'} = J_{\Psi'}^\top (J_{\Psi'} J_{\Psi'}^\top)^{-1}$. The loss penalty also enforces the wrong normal equation. Hence the construction does not realize the intended orthogonal projection.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula with the correct right inverse and use a loss such as $\|J_{\Psi'}J_\Psi - I_n\|^2$ to enforce the projection property.
issues.overall_effect: The A-stability analysis that relies on this projection is not valid as written.
issues.title: Incorrect formula for orthogonal projection decoder
issues.why_classification: The error is local but affects a key construction in the stability analysis; correcting it requires changing both the formula and the penalty.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We now assume the construction of an autoencoder that realizes an orthogonal projection.

issues.failure_explanation: Even if $P=J_\Psi J_{\Psi'}$ is an orthogonal projection onto $V$, the eigenvalues of $P\Lambda$ restricted to $V$ are not generally eigenvalues of $\Lambda$ unless $V$ is $\Lambda$-invariant. Counterexample: $\Lambda=\begin{bmatrix}-1&10\\0&-2\end{bmatrix}$ and $V=\operatorname{span}([1,1]^T)$. Then $P\Lambda$ on $V$ has eigenvalue $3.5$, while $\Lambda$ has eigenvalues $-1,-2$. Thus the reduced system can be unstable even if the original is stable.

failure_location.quote: Due to the specific assumptions made in the construction of the decoder, the projection sets some eigenvalues to zero while leaving the others unchanged. Therefore, the eigenvalues $\neq 0$ are those of $\Lambda$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the latent subspace to be $\Lambda$-invariant, or use a different stability analysis. This is a major additional assumption.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the reduced timestep bound is at worst the same as the full system is false in general. The A-stability guarantee for orthogonal-projection autoencoders is not established.
issues.title: Orthogonal projection does not preserve eigenvalues of the full system
issues.why_classification: The advertised stability preservation fails in general; a comparable result would require a strong invariant-subspace condition, changing the scope of the claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A necessary condition to meet the requirement $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\tau_n^k, \zeta_k \to 0$ and $\kappa \to 0$.
Given the assumption $\mathscr{J}_i=0$, we set $\mathscr{N}_{ij}^3 = 0$. Then, setting \eqref{eq:what_nn_learns_1} to zero and comparing it to \eqref{eq:diff_op_tau}, we conclude that

issues.failure_explanation: The proof only identifies necessary conditions by comparing residuals. It does not prove that $N_{F_n}$ converges to $F_n$. In fact, the difference between $N_{F_n}$ and $F_n$ involves dividing by $\Delta t$, so errors in $\zeta$ and $\kappa$ may be amplified rather than vanish. Thus the proposition's convergence claim is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: The fully data-driven is a convergent method for training $N_{F_n}$ in the sense that, under proper conditions, $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a rigorous convergence proof for the inverse problem, or replace the claim with a direct assumption that $N_{F_n}$ uniformly approximates $F_n$ with controlled error.
issues.overall_effect: The global convergence theorem's proof relies on this proposition to conclude $\varepsilon_{F_n}\to 0$ for fully data-driven training. Without it, the main convergence guarantee for the fully data-driven method is not established.
issues.title: Unsupported convergence claim for fully data-driven training
issues.why_classification: This undermines the main global convergence result for the fully data-driven approach; a new nontrivial argument or stronger assumption is required.
